questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Rational Function With Two Linear Factors as a Sum of Partial Fractions
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $B$ such that

$$
\frac{3x+5}{(x-3)(2x+1)}=\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{B}{2x+1}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(x-3)(2x+1)$ gives

$$
3x+5=2(2x+1)+B(x-3).
$$

For $x=-\frac{1}{2}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-\frac{1}{2})+5 & =2(2(-\frac{1}{2})+1)+B(-\frac{1}{2}-3) \\ \frac{7}{2} & =-\frac{7}{2}B \\ B & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{3x+5}{(x-3)(2x+1)}=\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{-1}{2x+1}.
$$

questions.problem:
Express $\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.

| $\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}=\,$ | {{field-1}} | $+$ | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $x$ |  | $x-1$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x-1}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $x(x-1)$ gives

$$
4-5x=A(x-1)+Bx.
$$

For $x=0$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5(0) & =A(0-1)+B(0) \\ 4 & =-A \\ A & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=1,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5(1) & =A(1-1)+B(1) \\ -1 & =B \\ B & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}=\frac{-4}{x}+\frac{-1}{x-1}.
$$

questions.problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{6x-25}{x(x+5)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{(x+5)},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are real constants, calculate $A+B.$
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6x-25}{x(x+5)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{(x+5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $x(x+5)$ gives

$$
6x-25=A(x+5)+B(x).
$$

For $x=0$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6(0)-25 & =A(0+5)+B(0) \\ -25 & =5A \\ A & =-\frac{25}{5} \\ A & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=-5$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6(-5)-25 & =A(-5+5)+B(-5) \\ -55 & =-5B \\ B & =\frac{-55}{-5} \\ B & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
A+B=-5+11=6.
$$

questions.problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{7x-37}{(5-3x)(2x+3)}=\frac{A}{(5-3x)}+\frac{B}{(2x+3)},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are real constants, calculate $A+B.$
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7x-37}{(5-3x)(2x+3)}=\frac{A}{(5-3x)}+\frac{B}{(2x+3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(5-3x)(2x+3)$ gives

$$
7x-37=A(2x+3)+B(5-3x).
$$

For $x=-\frac{3}{2}$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}7(-\frac{3}{2})-37 & =A(2(-\frac{3}{2})+3)+B(5-3(-\frac{3}{2})) \\ \frac{-21-74}{2} & =B(\frac{10+9}{2}) \\ \frac{-95}{2} & =B(\frac{19}{2}) \\ B & =\frac{-95}{19} \\ B & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=\frac{5}{3}$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}7(\frac{5}{3})-37 & =A(2(\frac{5}{3})+3)+B(5-3(\frac{5}{3})) \\ \frac{35-111}{3} & =A(\frac{10+9}{3}) \\ A & =\frac{-76}{19} \\ A & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
A+B=-4+(-5)=-4-5=-9.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ such that

$$
\frac{5x+11}{(x+1)(x+3)}=\frac{A}{x+1}+\frac{2}{x+3}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(x+1)(x+3)$ gives

$$
5x+11=A(x+3)+2(x+1).
$$

For $x=-1$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-1)+11 & =A(-1+3)+2(-1+1) \\ 6 & =2A \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{5x+11}{(x+1)(x+3)}=\frac{3}{x+1}+\frac{2}{x+3}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\dfrac{2x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\dfrac{2x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)} = \dfrac{A}{(x+2)} +\dfrac{B}{(x-3)}.
$$

Multiplying the above expression through by $(x+2)(x-3)$ gives

$$
2x-1= A(x-3)+B(x+2).
$$

Plugging in $x=-2$ gets rid of the $B$ term and allows us to solve for $A.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-2)-1 & =A(-2-3)+B(-2+2) \\ -5 & =A(-5)+B(0) \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=3$ gets rid of the $A$ term and allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(3)-1 & =A(3-3)+B(3+2) \\ 5 & =A(0)+B(5) \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Knowing that $A=1$ and $B=1,$ we have

$$
\dfrac{2x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)} = \dfrac{1}{(x+2)} +\dfrac{1}{(x-3)}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\dfrac{2x^2+5x+7}{(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\dfrac{2x^2+5x+7}{(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)} = \dfrac{A}{x+2} + \dfrac{B}{x-3} + \dfrac{C}{x+1}.
$$

First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)$ to clear the fractions:

$$
2x^2+5x+7= A(x-3)(x+1)+B(x+2)(x+1)+C(x+2)(x-3)
$$

Plugging in $x=-2$ gets rid of the $B$ and $C$ terms and allows us to solve for $A.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-2)^{2}+5(-2)+7 & =A(-2-3)(-2+1) \\ 5 & =A(5) \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=3$ gets rid of the $A$ and $C$ terms and allows us to solve for $B.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(3)^{2}+5(3)+7 & =B(3+2)(3+1) \\ 40 & =B(20) \\ B & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, plugging in $x=-1$ gets rid of the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)^{2}+5(-1)+7 & =C(-1+2)(-1-3) \\ 4 & =C(-4) \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Knowing that $A=1,$ $B=2,$ and $C=-1,$ we have

$$
\dfrac{2x^2+5x+7}{(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)} = \dfrac{1}{x+2} +\dfrac{2}{x-3} -\dfrac{1}{x+1}.
$$
